title: A Travel Blogger's Story
description: Four recordings about a travel blogger: an interview, a story about a bad day, two friends planning a trip and a travel fair announcement.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · An interview
parts.intro: You will hear a radio presenter, Tom, interviewing a travel blogger called Sophie.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Joining me today is Sophie Lane, a travel blogger whose stories are read by thousands of people. Sophie, how did it all start?

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: By accident, really. Four years ago I took a gap year and wrote emails to my family about my trip. My aunt said I should put them online, so I started a blog.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: And was it popular straight away?

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: No, nobody read it for months. My only reader was my aunt! Then one of my photos, a tiny market in the mountains, went viral, and suddenly I had ten thousand followers.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Do you now travel full time?

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: Almost. I'm away about eight months of the year. I don't earn a fortune, but companies pay me to write about hotels and tours, and that covers my costs.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: What's the hardest part of the job?

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: People think I'm always on the beach. In reality, I spend a lot of time on buses and in airports, and writing late at night. It's tiring.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Where are you going next?

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: Vietnam. I'm very excited. I've heard the food is amazing.

parts.title: Part 2 · A bad day in Portugal
parts.intro: You will hear Sophie telling a story from her blog.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: I'd like to tell you about the day everything went wrong, on a trip to Portugal last year. It started well. I'd planned to take a small train to a village on the coast, and I was very proud because I'd booked everything weeks in advance.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: When I arrived at the station, I realised I'd left my ticket in my hotel room. The man at the desk wasn't very helpful. I had to buy a new one, which cost me twelve euros.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: The train was twenty minutes late, and then it stopped in the middle of nowhere for an hour. Everyone was cross, but an old lady shared her oranges with me, and we chatted in a mixture of English and Portuguese.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: At last I reached the village, but the hotel I'd booked was closed for repairs. Nobody had told me. I stood in the street with my heavy bag, feeling quite miserable.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: Then the old lady appeared again. She was visiting her sister, and she took me home for dinner. They gave me a bed for the night, and the next morning her sister showed me the best beach in the area, which isn't in any guidebook.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.text: That unlucky day became the best story on my blog. People often ask me where to go. My answer is: go anywhere, but expect problems, because problems make the best memories.

parts.title: Part 3 · Planning a trip
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Lily and Jake, talking about a blog post.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Jake, have you seen Sophie's latest blog post about Vietnam? She says we should avoid the big tourist places.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: Really? But I wanted to see Ha Long Bay. Everybody says it's beautiful.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: She says it is, but it's crowded in summer. Her advice is to go in spring or autumn.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: That's not possible for me. I can only travel in July because of my work.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Then she suggests taking an early boat, before eight o'clock, when there are fewer people.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: OK, that's something. What else does she recommend?

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Staying with local families instead of hotels. It's cheaper and you learn more about daily life.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: Hmm. I'm not sure. I like having my own bathroom, to be honest.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Don't be so fussy! But she also says we should take the night train from the capital to the north. It's slow, but you save a night in a hotel.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: Now that I like. How long does it take?

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: About eight hours. We could sleep most of the way.

script.speaker: Jake
script.text: All right, you've convinced me. Send me the link, and I'll start planning tonight.

parts.title: Part 4 · A travel fair
parts.intro: You will hear a radio announcement about a travel fair.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: This is a reminder from Radio Wanderer about this weekend's Travel Fair at the city exhibition centre.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: The fair opens on Saturday at ten and closes at six. On Sunday it opens an hour later, at eleven, and closes at five.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Tickets cost eight pounds at the door, but if you buy online you pay only six. Children under twelve go in free, and students get a discount of two pounds with a student card.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: During the fair, there will be more than fifty talks. The most popular is by blogger Sophie Lane, on Saturday at two o'clock, about her trip around Vietnam. Seats are limited, so we advise you to arrive early.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: There will also be a photography competition. Bring your best travel photo, printed, and leave it at the main desk before noon on Saturday. The winner receives a flight for two to a European city.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Please don't drive if you can avoid it. Parking is limited and expensive, but there's a bus every ten minutes from the central station.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: We look forward to seeing you there, and happy travels.
